# NOVA MART Attack–Defense

SSH/console account: `user-access`. Your organizer gives your team password. Per-service web URLs are in `~/lab-addresses.txt` on your VM. Each team receives an isolated instance.

- team01 identity page: http://10.80.0.11/
  - NOVA MART · Round 1: http://10.80.0.11:8080/
  - NOVA MART · Round 2: http://10.80.0.11:8081/
- team02 identity page: http://10.80.0.12/
  - NOVA MART · Round 1: http://10.80.0.12:8080/
  - NOVA MART · Round 2: http://10.80.0.12:8081/
- team03 identity page: http://10.80.0.13/
  - NOVA MART · Round 1: http://10.80.0.13:8080/
  - NOVA MART · Round 2: http://10.80.0.13:8081/
- team04 identity page: http://10.80.0.14/
  - NOVA MART · Round 1: http://10.80.0.14:8080/
  - NOVA MART · Round 2: http://10.80.0.14:8081/

New connections from attacker VMs to the shared server 10.80.0.20 are blocked. The router is 10.80.0.1.

The service is NOVA MART, an intentionally vulnerable web shop. Challenge paths: SQL injection in product search; CAPTCHA bypass; stored XSS in reviews; CSRF in order sharing; and weak merchant credentials with no effective rate limit. Order private notes hold short-lived flags. The functional checker creates one flag per team/service/tick, checks the current and still-active orders, and awards SLA only when that flow works.

Event schedule: 2 rounds × 30 minutes; 120 seconds/tick; 15 ticks/round. UP earns 1 SLA point; missed/DOWN/MUMBLE earns zero. A captured active flag earns 100 points and its owner loses 100. Flag lifetime: 3 ticks.

For external access, the organizer runs Configure-Deployment.ps1 after allocation and publishes the generated gateway URLs and scoreboard. The read-only operations monitor has its own token.

Enter `finish-idor-lab` when done.
